rows.note: The corrected flow of the merged runbook (lines a to f, one host$ line per step file): the guest reboots inside the same QEMU process. The steps script waits for no QEMU exit and re-launches nothing; between t8-a-reboot.sh and t8-b-wait-boot-id.sh it only waits, read-only, for the same guest to answer with another boot id (no row file). Each step file is sourced in its own shell, so the steps script sets T8 to the value the step before left (rebooting, rebooted, returned, reconnected, ok), and only when that step printed no STOP: (runbook lines 1493-1495); each of the five later step files, sourced without it, refuses and runs nothing. A STOP: in a step ends the row there: no later step file is run, and t9 is not run.

Each of t9-a, t9-b, t9-c, t9-de only if the one before printed no STOP:. t9-exposure.sh is the prose-only step of runbook line 1537; the steps script runs it likewise only if t9-de printed no STOP: (runbook line 15), so after a STOP of (d)+(e) the three read-only exposure reads are not in the package.

t8-a-reboot.sh.range_note: Line a: the command of line 1486 with its nine continuation lines 1487-1495, which the rule keeps: they are comments (QEMU runs without -no-reboot and the guest reboots inside the same QEMU process; nothing is re-launched; T8 carries the test's state between its lines) and run nothing. The prefix stands 15 times, all on line 1486.

t8-b-wait-boot-id.sh.range_note: Line b, line 1496: the boot id read again and again, each read bounded by 'timeout 20' and counted only at exit status 0, until it differs from the saved one (REBOOT SHOWN). It refuses unless T8=rebooting, the value line a leaves in its own shell.

t8-d-tunnel.sh.range_note: Line d, line 1498: tunnel_down and tunnel_up. It refuses unless T8=returned. Nothing is substituted: the line holds no id.

t8-e-state.sh.range_note: Line e, line 1499: wait_ready 3600, the post-reboot /metrics reading and twin snapshot, 'same', CONTROLLER PROCESS NEW. It refuses unless T8=reconnected. With the 15, 8 and 32 of lines 1486, 1496 and 1497 these are the sixty literals of T8's prefix, changed together.

t8-f-smoke.sh.range_note: Line f, line 1500: the post-reboot smoke, started only when T8=ok.

Line ranges. A step file holds each host$ command whole, with its continuation lines (trailing comment lines), so its source_line_numbers are the lines of the text. Where the lines on which commands START and the text differ the file's range_note says why.
Every line the rule extracts under the two headings stands in exactly one step file (41 extracted lines: 15 of test 8, 26 of test 9; 41 lines in the ten runbook step files).

A command is cut between two files only before trailing comment lines (asserted): lines 1511-1522 (after the command of line 1510), 1525 (after 1524) and 1528-1530 (after 1527). Comments run nothing. Test 8's comment lines 1487-1495 stay with the command they continue (line 1486, t8-a-reboot.sh).

Test 8, the corrected flow (the block was rewritten on 2026-10-03 after session S2's halt and merged as 8e49261): six host$ lines, a to f, one step file each. The launcher runs QEMU without -no-reboot and the guest reboots inside the same QEMU process: no line waits for a QEMU exit and nothing is re-launched. The lines carry the test's state in the shell variable T8 (rebooting after a, rebooted after b, returned after c, reconnected after d, ok after e) and each advances it only on success; the step files are sourced in separate shells, so the driver sets T8 to the value the step before left, and only when that step printed no STOP: (runbook lines 1493-1495).

Test 9's fenced block has the family hash the battery's extraction asserted on the blob of 80e833f (9518fefe751c3d93, asserted here as well): the same ten commands and twenty-six lines, 8 lines lower (1509-1534, then 1501-1526). The sentence of the exposure step stands on line 1537 (then 1529).

Not extracted, by the rule: line 1508 (a comment before the first host$ line of test 9's fence) and line 1260 (the section's preamble under '## 7.', outside the two headings: it sources ~/egw-tcg/.env and ~/egw-tcg/itest-helpers.sh). The steps script's hx runs a superset of it, HOST_PRE of the clean clone's tools/session/guest_common.sh: the execution venv activated, ~/egw-tcg/.env exported, EGW_CLONE set to the clean clone, the DEPLOYED ~/egw-tcg/itest-helpers.sh and ~/egw-tcg/tunnel.sh sourced (files of the host, not of the clone), and the tunnel checked or reopened.

The step files of kind 'runbook' hold the extracted lines and nothing else: no header, no added line. The prose-only file is a constant of the script and opens with the runbook sentence it derives from.

A <file>.diff is the unified diff (no context lines) between the extracted text and the step file; its line numbers count the lines of the extracted text, and the header names the runbook lines. It is empty when the file has no substitution; the prose-only file has none.
Every file is UTF-8 with LF line endings and one final newline, and passed 'bash -n'.

Independent check: g3_check_rows.sh (beside this script) restates the line ranges and the ids on its own and compares each runbook step file, with every '-q2' removed, byte for byte with the blob's lines, cut with 'awk' and 'sed'. It reads the blob from the clean clone with 'git show' (and then also requires that clone at 8e49261 and clean), or, before the clone has moved to that commit, from a file given with --blob whose sha256 it asserts (it then shows nothing about the clone).
